# Syrtis v0.6.0

**This release brings Windows level with the macOS app's screens, adds Simplified Chinese, and adds an opt-in Discord status.** Nothing you already use changes unless you turn it on.

## Show today's usage on Discord

Syrtis can now show what you have been building today on your Discord profile, the way games show what you are playing. **It is off until you turn it on**, in Settings → General → Discord.

- You choose what appears: today's tokens, the tool you used most (or one tool you pick), and your spend as a range such as $10–50. Exact whole-dollar amounts are a separate opt-in, and cents are never shown.
- Tools you have hidden from the tab row never appear, not even in the totals.
- Anyone who can see your Discord profile can see it. Turning it off stops further updates; it cannot take back what was already shown.
- A short card introduces the feature once. It only opens Settings; nothing is turned on for you.

## New to the screens

- **Brand icons** for Claude, Codex, Copilot, Antigravity, Grok and other tools, on the tab row, the Agent limits card, the past-windows list and the Settings tab list.
- **A Chart layout for the Agent limits card** (Settings → Dashboard → Agent limits → Layout: Chart). Each window is drawn as a curve over time with the pace estimate as a second line. Windows without recorded history keep the bar.
- **API-list-price equivalent on the Stats page**, split by the subscription each tool is counted toward, with "Not a subscription" and "Unassigned" shown separately.
- **Font color for the tray value** (Settings → Menu bar → Font color). Pick your own colors for normal, low and very low remaining quota, from 16 presets or any hex value.
- **Simplified Chinese** (简体中文) as a language option.
- **A new app icon** with the same shape and soft shading.

## Also in this release

- The usage engine is updated. Where you have the data: OpenCode 2.x usage now appears, OpenClaw archives are counted and its checkpoints are no longer counted twice, Grok usage is kept when a log has a damaged line, Cursor cache-write tokens are counted separately, a Cursor row reported at $0.00 shows $0, and Cline 4.x is priced under its real model. Claude and Codex figures do not change. The first scan after updating takes longer while those tools' records are read again.
- A Codex sign-in is now refreshed when its access token is about to expire, not only once it is eight days old.
- When GitHub is rate-limiting update checks, Settings says so instead of a generic "Could not check for updates."
